EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  JANUARY 28, 2019

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN HUFF called the meeting to order, the time being 7:03 p.m. in the Rolling Hills
Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Britt Huff
Valerie Ciarolla
Patricia Harik
Carrie Silvano
Vicki Shinn

COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT
Susan Brtis
Carol Dean-Porter
Bill Kemp
Tim Zigrang

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 26, 2018
MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE NOVEMBER 26, 2018 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN HUFF SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
Pam Schachter, 46 Ranchview Road, requested on the behalf of a licensed horse trainer for
the City to consider adding a manual arena sprinkler control button on the junior dressage
arena in Dapplegray Park. The Community Services Director indicated that he would
investigate this inquiry and place this item on the Equestrian Committee’s next meeting
agenda.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JANUARY 28, 2019  1
 CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT MONTHLY
UPDATE
Korey Bradbury from California Water Service Company distributed project update fact sheets
and highlighted the progress made thus far. He indicated that most of the work was currently
taking place near the Rolling Hills United Methodist Church and that this section of the project
would likely be completed by mid-February.

Carmelo Sorce, Project Manager, reported that unanticipated lateral sewer lines from the
mainline sewer pipe in the Palomino Ranchos Trail to nearby homes were discovered and has
required a review of alternatives resulting in the development of new plans to replace and
encase the lateral lines in concrete. This would allow them to hold the weight of the new
water pipeline to be installed above them (rather than under the lateral sewer lines) and the
weight of vehicles using this trail. The revised scope of work will delay this project from being
completed in March 2019 to June 2019. The new water pipe will be placed two feet under the
trail surface and audience members living near this trail cautioned Mr. Sorce that the new pipe
may become exposed during heavy rainstorms from trail surface erosion. In response to
inquiries, Mr. Sorce stated that California Water Service Company would be responsible to
replace any eroded trail material to cover the pipe and would rely on equestrians, nearby
residents, and City staff to inform him when this occurs.

Audience member, Chris Wolf, expressed her concerns that the completion of the project
along the Palomino Ranchos Trail continues to be delayed. CHAIRMAN HUFF responded
that until a trail is trenched, it’s often unknown what will be found in the soil. She also
requested that the reasons for the project delays be put up on the City’s website.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN HUFF THANKED MR. BRADBURY AND MR.
SORCE AND RECEIVED AND FILED THIS AGENDA ITEM.

HOWLETT PARK RIDING CLINIC CONFLICTS WITH ADJACENT ARENA USERS
The Community Services Director thanked Subcommittee Members who met twice since the
last Equestrian Committee meeting to develop recommendations for the Committee’s
consideration. He reviewed all of the potential alternatives developed by the Subcommittee
regarding the issue of turning out of horses at this multi-arena, public equestrian center.

Audience member, Pam Schachter, noted that the City’s horse arena regulations indicate that
arena users must cooperate and be considerate of other riders. MEMBER SILVANO stated
that the equestrian community is fortunate that the City has provided so many horse arenas
for the public to enjoy. She also noted that the annual Licensed Horse Trainers meeting
would be held soon to explain this new policy and that if trainers did not accommodate riders
needing to turn out a horse for a few minutes at Howlett Park, then this inappropriate behavior
could result in their Business License being suspended or revoked. Audience member, Chris
Wolf, inquired about what a trainer would do when more than one request to turn out a horse
during an hour lesson. MEMBER SILVANO responded that this would not likely happen often
and that some trainers actually like horses to be ridden or turned out in adjacent arenas when
they give lessons.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JANUARY 28, 2019  2
 MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO APPROVE: 1) THE NOTIFICATION OF CLINIC ORGANIZERS AND LICENSED
  HORSE TRAINERS BY CITY STAFF THAT IF THEY ARE UNWILLING TO ALLOW A
  RIDER TEN MINUTES TO TURN OUT A HORSE DURING THEIR SESSIONS AT
  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK, THEY MUST RENT THE ADJACENT ARENA(S); AND 2)
  CITY STAFF WILL POST SIGNS ON ADJACENT ARENAS WHEN CLINICS ARE
  HELD AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK INDICATING THAT RIDING ONLY IS ALLOWED
  (NO TURN OUTS) WHILE A CLINIC IS IN SESSION.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN HUFF SO ORDERED.

ANNUAL LICENSED HORSE TRAINERS MANDATORY MEETING DATE
The Community Services Director recommended and the Committee agreed that this meeting
be held prior to the next scheduled Equestrian Committee meeting at 6:00 p.m. on Monday,
February 25, 2019 in the City Hall Council Chambers, as has been held in prior years. All
licensed horse trainers would be notified of the meeting by mail. Audience member, Pam
Schachter, requested that Chandler Park trainers be reminded that beginner riding lessons
can more safely take place in the Pepperwood Park arena.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN HUFF SO ORDERED.

EQUINE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS SUBCOMMITTEE UPDATE
MEMBER SHINN provided an overview of the Subcommittee’s progress on: 1) establishing
preliminary equine evacuation sites throughout the City in the event of a fire; 2) the need to
have equine supply containers at these sites; and 3) how equestrians will endeavor should an
earthquake or other disaster damage water lines to the PV Peninsula. MEMBER SILVANO
reported that the City was developing a horse census survey which would be helpful to the
Subcommittee’s understanding of where horses are located in the City.

Gil Houle, Peter Weber Equestrian Center Concession Operator, reported that he had two
300-gallon water storage units and was investigating the addition of a 1,000-gallon unit. He
volunteered to coordinate a future workshop at his venue for equestrians to learn about the
various types of water storage units that are available in today’s market.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN HUFF RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

PROPOSED PI CHARITY RACE COURSE REQUEST
The Community Services Director introduced local student, Connor Spencer and his mother,
noting that the Park and Activities Commission had previously approved his past three races
that had taken place in, or mostly occurred, in Ernie Howlett Park. Proceeds from this race
are donated to Heifer International and Doctors Without Borders.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JANUARY 28, 2019  3
 Connor Spencer has requested that the March 10, 2019 Race allow runners to leave the park
on the City’s trails and make a loop around the City Hall/Pepperwood Park/Chandler Park site
before returning back to Howlett Park. Staff expressed concerns about runners going past
Chandler Park’s arena while riding lessons were occurring, as well as, closing the trails in that
area of the City during the mid-morning peak time use of Chandler and Pepperwood Park’s
arenas.

MEMBER SHINN suggested that the race course utilize the Palos Verdes Landfill instead.
Connor Spencer concurred and the Community Services Director stated that he would assist
in obtaining the permits from Los Angeles County for use of the landfill’s trails.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN HUFF SO ORDERED.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
The Community Services Director noted that the portable restroom at Dapplegray Park had
been recently replaced.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN HUFF RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS

MEMBER SHINN reported increased equestrian crossings at Crenshaw Boulevard and Palos
Verdes Drive North due to the Botanical Gardens Trail closing near the Rolling Hills United
Methodist Church. She requested a “Horses Crossing” warning sign be installed on
Crenshaw Boulevard near the intersection. The Community Services Director stated that a
sign would be immediately installed.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN HUFF RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

A.  PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT UPDATE – Monthly

B.  EQUINE EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN UPDATE – Monthly

C.  COYOTE ISSUES (February 25, 2019)

  (February 25, 2019)

E.  PROPOSED CHANDLER PARK ROUND PEN (February 25, 2019)

F.  EQUESTRIAN FEES (March 25, 2019)
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JANUARY 28, 2019  4
 G.  BROWN ACT REVIEW (March 25, 2019)

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN HUFF ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 8:17 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
